key_decisions: THE UMBRELLA ORDER CHANGED. MPI-375 (Paint) is third, MPI-368 (Shapes) fourth. Shapes is ONE gizmo with TWO destinations and Paint builds the second one, so Shapes-first could only have shipped half of itself. tasks/MPI-424/brief.md holds the rationale.

EXTRACT THE DAB, NOT A CLASS. brushDab.js is stampDab() + strokeDabs(); MaskManager stamps it twice (manual + subtract), PaintManager once. A full BrushEngine was rejected - it would rewrite a working shared primitive and every call site for nothing extra. MPI-435 parameterises stampDab and BOTH brushes get textures. If a change ever edits two dab implementations, the extraction regressed - repair it, do not fork.

PAINT PERSISTS PER ENTRY, like masks (temp PNG). Decided because the headline flow is paint -> mask -> detail, which SPANS a tool switch; discard-on-exit breaks it at step one. This is item 4 and is NOT built yet.

PAINT IS COMMITTED PIXELS, NOT A PREVIEW. It does NOT extend discardPreview(). The preview contract exists to stop an UNCOMMITTED preview outliving its tool; a paint stroke is as committed as a manualCanvas brush stroke.

OPACITY IS DISPLAY OPACITY, not paint alpha - same meaning the slider already has for the mask. Marked with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling: true alpha painting needs a per-stroke scratch buffer, because dabs overlap 75% and would build to solid within one stroke (slow drag darker than a fast one).

ONE UndoStack, chronological, shared by mask and paint. Accepted consequence, documented in MpiCanvas: Ctrl+Z inside Paint can walk back into a mask stroke. One canvas, one history; a second stack was ruled out before undo was built.
PAINT LAYER IS IMAGE-NATIVE, capped at PAINT_MAX_EDGE 4096 - not the mask's 1536. It becomes REAL pixels in a new entry, so downscale-then-upscale would soften every stroke.

AGENTS DO NOT EDIT WORKFLOW JSON (unchanged, still true). The user edits comfy_workflows/raw/ by hand; the agent produces the LIST (raw file, node id, widget INDEX) and runs scripts/sync-raw-workflows.mjs.
constraints: A PRE-EXISTING MASK-BRUSH BUG WAS FIXED ON THE WAY THROUGH. MaskManager.paint() stamped one arc per mousemove with nothing joining them, so any drag faster than the brush is wide left holes (40 image-px at the default). It read as a skipping brush, not a missing feature. The shared interpolation closes it for BOTH brushes. This is a USER-VISIBLE change to a shipped tool and owes UNRELEASED.md its own line.

THE HALF-WIRE THAT ALMOST SHIPPED, and the guard that now catches it: MpiCanvasViewer._enterMode() was a hardcoded if(crop)/else if(mask)/else chain, so 'paint' fell through to activeMode='none'. NOTHING FAILED - the button worked, the panel mounted, and the canvas just panned on drag. A dead tool that looks alive. It is now a CANVAS_MODES set, and tests/mask-tool-registry.test.cjs ties _viewerModeFor's outputs to the viewer's accepted modes. Adding a canvas mode means adding it to CANVAS_MODES and _syncModeFromCanvas, nowhere else.
MpiCanvas._methods is an ALLOWLIST. A missing name is undefined on el, and the optional-call idiom in the panels swallows it in total silence. The paint methods are already in it.

MpiMaskStrip is now SHARED by two families and driven by its DESTINATIONS table. Adding a destination is adding a ROW, never a branch in setup(). A missing row silently falls back to 'mask', so a paint tool would drive the MASK layer while looking correct - there is a guard for this.
Tests run as node --test with the QUOTED glob "tests/*.test.cjs". The directory form dies on Node v24. Suite is at 336/0 (was 329 at session start; 324 before the MPI-434 peer session).

THE WORKING TREE IS CRLF and it bit this session for real: a new guard anchored on ';\n' matched nothing and read as 'the constant was renamed'. Use ';\r?\n'. Always assert a sabotage APPLIED before trusting a negative control - five fired this session, all restored byte-identical.

SOURCE-TEXT TESTS CANNOT PROVE PIXEL LOGIC. The real-pixel route is a temp module under js/ served same-origin off the running :3000, imported in Chromium via playwright-cli, deleted after. 32 assertions ran that way this session. NOTE: playwright-cli eval has NO --file flag - pass the expression inline as an async IIFE - and it CACHES ES modules, so busting the probe URL is not enough; close and reopen the page to pick up an edited dependency.
